criteria.text: Reviews entry screen is the landing view with a Next up start card and a Published list.
criteria.note: The landing view shows a 'NEXT UP' pill over 'August 2026', a '5 buckets · 19 KPIs · Source: DX Scorecard (live)' meta, a green 'Pull data & start' button and a '~30s · re-pullable anytime' hint. Beneath, a PUBLISHED list has 'July 2026' with a lock icon, a green 'Published' chip, '19 KPIs · locked Jul 28, 2026' and a 'View' button.
criteria.impactWhy: The Reviews entry screen is high because the whole MBR flow starts from it and the mission depends on it being the landing view.
criteria.reason: Impact high because the flow starts here. I opened #mbr; I saw the start card and Published row exactly as specified (evidence: mbr-start). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Collection screen shows each bucket cycling to 'N values pulled' behind a progress bar, with Cancel and a Continue-to-builder button disabled until the pull finishes.
criteria.note: At #mbr/collect a full-width progress bar sits above a list of five buckets, each ending in a green 'N values pulled' chip (all read '0 values pulled' here because every KPI is manual). A 'Cancel' control sits bottom-left and a green 'Continue to builder' button bottom-right, enabled at the finished state.
criteria.impactWhy: The collection screen is high because the pull is the entry gate to the builder and the mission's flow depends on it.
criteria.reason: Impact high because the pull gates the builder. I opened #mbr/collect; I saw the progress bar, bucket 'values pulled' chips, Cancel and an enabled Continue at completion (evidence: mbr-collect). The mid-pull cycling and disabled transient were not captured, but nothing contradicts the spec. Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Builder matches the mockup: eyebrow, 'MBR builder · {month}' title, exact subtitle, a Preview button and an amber 'Lock month' button.
criteria.note: The head shows the eyebrow 'MONTHLY BUSINESS REVIEW', title 'MBR builder · September 2026', the exact subtitle sentence, a 'Preview' toolbar button and an amber 'Lock month' primary button.
criteria.impactWhy: The builder head and toolbar are high because the builder is the core surface the mission rebuilds.
criteria.reason: Impact high because the builder is the core surface. I opened #mbr/build; I saw the eyebrow, title, subtitle, Preview and amber Lock month button (evidence: mbr-build). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Draft banner is amber with a warning dot, 'Draft — changes are saved locally as you go', a 'Last edited {t} · N of M buckets complete' meta and a 'Discard draft' button.
criteria.note: An amber banner with a warning dot reads 'Draft — changes are saved locally as you go.', with a 'Last edited — · 3 of 5 buckets complete' meta and a 'Discard draft' button on its right.
criteria.impactWhy: The draft banner is medium because it is a stated requirement but secondary to the builder's core add-insight-and-lock purpose.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because it is a secondary status affordance. I opened #mbr/build; I saw the amber banner, dot, text, meta and Discard draft button (evidence: mbr-build). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Refresh-all lives in an amber warning box stating it only collects automated KPIs ('11 of 14'), leaves manual KPIs unchanged, and drives an indeterminate progress strip.
criteria.note: The amber refresh-all warning box is not present anywhere on the builder page (measured: automateBtn present:false, bulkBar present:false). Every one of the 19 KPIs in this build's data is manual (the collect screen shows '6 manual', '3 manual', '2 manual', '3 manual', '5 manual'), so the automatable partition is empty and I cannot tell whether the box is correctly suppressed for a zero-automatable month or missing.
criteria.impactWhy: Refresh-all is medium because it is a stated convenience but secondary to the per-KPI collect and manual editing the mission centres on.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because it is a secondary sweep control. I looked for the warn box on #mbr/build and read the element boxes; I saw no box and no automate button, but the data has zero automatable KPIs so its absence may be correct. Outcome: couldn't check (unobservable).

criteria.text: An 'Insights added — N of M KPIs' completion bar sits under the banner; done = non-empty insight, and reaching all KPIs is the month-lockable condition.
criteria.note: Under the banner a bar reads 'Insights added' with '16 of 19 KPIs' at its right. The lock dialog confirms the same gate: '16 of 19 KPIs have an insight · 3 still empty. Every KPI needs an insight before this month can be locked.'
criteria.impactWhy: The completion bar is high because it is the lock gate the whole publish flow hinges on.
criteria.reason: Impact high because the meter is the lock gate. I read the completion bar and the lock dialog summary; both show 16 of 19 and tie completion to non-empty insights (evidence: mbr-build). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Per-KPI status is an editable select over five silhouettes; the off-track marker is an X shape distinct from the on-track circle.
criteria.note: Each KPI row carries an editable status select listing On track / Watch / Off track / Tracking / WIP. Off-track rows (e.g. '% Agentic Fix PRs merged', 'Core 4 Availability') show a red X marker, visibly a crossed shape unlike the filled on-track circle on 'Codespaces Startup Time'.
criteria.impactWhy: Per-KPI editorial status is high because it is a core builder capability and the X/circle distinction is an explicit design requirement.
criteria.reason: Impact high because status editing and the X shape are core. I read the KPI rows on #mbr/build and the locked view; I saw the five-option select and X markers on off-track KPIs distinct from the circle (evidence: mbr-build). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Value/target/delta arrive with the pull; delta is always computed and manual edits recompute delta automatically; deltas are never hand-typed.
criteria.note: Each KPI cell shows a value, a 'target N' line and a 'vs last MBR' delta (all '0' here since every KPI is carried against the identical prior MBR). Deltas render as read-only text, not inputs.
criteria.impactWhy: Value/target/delta plumbing is high because the review's numbers are the substance of the MBR.
criteria.reason: Impact high because the numbers are the MBR's substance. I read the value cells on #mbr/build; I saw value, target and a non-editable 'vs last MBR' delta on every row (evidence: mbr-build). The edit-recompute path is internal and covered separately (t-009-ac3). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Manual KPIs are edited inline (unit, target, delta, 'From default view · edit to override' note, 'Manual' tag, amber 'needs value' state) with no lock/asOf step.
criteria.note: Manual rows show an editable value input with its unit, a 'target N' line, a 'vs last MBR' delta, a 'From default view · edit to override' note and an amber 'MANUAL' tag; empty inputs (e.g. Codespaces Startup Time, Copilot SRE Impact Score) take an amber treatment.
criteria.impactWhy: Manual inline editing is medium because it is a required editing model but supports rather than defines the core review flow.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because it is a supporting editing model. I read the manual KPI cells on #mbr/build; I saw inline inputs, unit, target, delta, the override note and the MANUAL tag (evidence: mbr-build). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Wired KPI value cells show value, target, a 'vs last MBR' delta, an 'Auto' tag and Collect / Re-collect / Try again controls with Collecting/Updated/failed chips and a 'was {old} · as of {date}' line.
criteria.note: No wired value cell appears anywhere in the builder: every one of the 19 KPIs is manual/carried (all rows carry a 'MANUAL' tag; none carry an 'Auto' tag or Collect control). With no automated KPI in the data I could not reach the Auto tag, the Collect/Re-collect/Try again controls or the collect-state chips.
criteria.impactWhy: Wired value cells are medium because they are a required automated-collect surface but secondary to the manual editing that carries this build's data.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because it is a secondary automated surface. I scanned every KPI row on #mbr/build for an Auto tag or Collect control; I saw only MANUAL rows, so no wired cell was reachable (the data has zero automatable KPIs). Outcome: couldn't check (unobservable).

criteria.text: Multi-value (cohort) KPIs show a per-source 'change vs last MBR' delta column with a 'change vs last MBR' caption.
criteria.note: Cohort KPIs (LTC P75, New Service Language Breakdown, Ci Critical Path Time) list each source as a label/value row with its own delta column and a 'change vs last MBR' caption beneath the list.
criteria.impactWhy: Cohort delta display is medium because it is a required detail for some KPIs but not the mission's central mechanism.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because it is a per-KPI detail. I read the cohort cells on #mbr/build; I saw per-source rows with a delta column and the 'change vs last MBR' caption (evidence: mbr-build). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Carried KPIs render a purple 'Carried' pill with a clock icon when the pull returns no fresh value.
criteria.note: Every KPI row shows a purple 'Carried' pill with a clock icon, consistent with a pull that returned zero fresh values (all buckets show '0 values pulled').
criteria.impactWhy: The Carried pill is medium because it is a required provenance cue but secondary to the values and insights themselves.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because it is a provenance cue. I read the KPI rows on #mbr/build; I saw purple Carried pills with a clock icon, matching the zero-fresh-value pull (evidence: mbr-build). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Bucket headers read 'N KPIs' with an 'N of M insights' sub-count and carry no per-bucket lock state, badge or unlock control.
criteria.note: Each bucket header reads a KPI count (e.g. 'Velocity 6 KPIs') with an 'N of M insights' sub-count on the right (e.g. '4 of 6 insights'), and carries no per-bucket lock badge or unlock control.
criteria.impactWhy: Bucket headers are medium because they are a required layout detail but not the point of the review.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because it is a layout detail. I read every bucket header on #mbr/build; I saw 'N KPIs' with 'N of M insights' and no per-bucket lock affordance (evidence: mbr-build). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Insights autosave on blur and debounced; a non-empty insight gets a distinct filled background; the whole draft persists to disk and the 'last edited' meta reflects the latest autosave.
criteria.note: Non-empty insight cells render the entered text (e.g. 'Remains under our 50%+ cut goal.') while empty ones show the 'Add an insight for this KPI…' placeholder, and there is no explicit save control. The preview screen renders the same draft insights, showing the draft state is retained.
criteria.impactWhy: Autosave/persistence is medium because it is a stated requirement that supports, but does not define, the add-insight-and-lock flow, and the visible draft/preview state shows the draft is retained.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because it supports the core flow. I read the insight cells on #mbr/build and the preview render; I saw filled non-empty cells, placeholder empties, no save button, and the draft carried through to preview (evidence: mbr-build). The PUT/debounce mechanism itself is internal (t-007-ac6). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Re-pull re-runs collection for automated KPIs only, recomputing their deltas; every manual value and insight is preserved; a KPI with no fresh value stays as it was.
criteria.note: Re-pull acts on automated KPIs, of which this build's data has none, and nothing on the screen shows the preserve/recompute behaviour. The provided test output tail lists 'scripts/mbr-refresh.test.ts (5 tests)' passing but does not quote a test line naming this behaviour, so I cannot cite it.
criteria.impactWhy: Re-pull is medium because it is a stated refresh behaviour secondary to the initial pull and manual editing.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because it is a secondary refresh path. I looked for a re-pull surface on #mbr/build and checked the test tail; I saw no automated KPI to re-pull and no quotable naming line. Outcome: couldn't check (unobservable).

criteria.text: Locking is per-month only; the lock dialog is 'Lock {Month Year}?' with a summary reflecting insight completeness and no 'Locked by' handle field, and blank insights block the lock.
criteria.note: The Lock month button opens a centered 'Lock September 2026?' dialog with an amber lock icon badge and the summary '16 of 19 KPIs have an insight · 3 still empty. Every KPI needs an insight before this month can be locked.' There is no 'Locked by' handle field.
criteria.impactWhy: Per-month locking is high because publishing the review is the mission's end goal and its gate.
criteria.reason: Impact high because publishing is the goal. I opened the lock dialog; I saw the month-scoped title, the insight-completeness summary, the blank-insight gate and no handle field (evidence: lock-dialog). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: When the month is locked all buckets render read-only: static values, status as a label, insight as text, editable again only by unlocking.
criteria.note: The locked July 2026 snapshot (#locked/2026-07-27.0) renders every bucket read-only: static values, status shown as a marker/label (no select), and insights shown as plain text (no textarea).
criteria.impactWhy: Locked read-only rendering is high because a published month must not be editable and that is a core correctness guarantee.
criteria.reason: Impact high because a published month must be static. I opened the locked July snapshot via View; I saw static values, label statuses and text insights with no editable controls (evidence: locked-view). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Dialogs (discard, lock, unlock-month) are centered overlays over a dimmed backdrop with a coloured icon badge, dismissable by backdrop click or Esc; discard is 'Discard this draft?' with a danger icon and Keep editing / Discard draft.
criteria.note: The discard dialog is a centered overlay over a dimmed backdrop with a red danger icon badge, 'Discard this draft?', a warning body and a 'Keep editing' / red 'Discard draft' pair; the lock dialog matches the same overlay pattern with an amber badge. The unlock dialog was not captured.
criteria.impactWhy: Dialog styling is medium because the dialogs are required affordances but secondary to the actions they confirm.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because dialogs support the actions. I opened the discard and lock dialogs; both are centered, dimmed-backdrop overlays with coloured icon badges and correct wording (evidence: discard-dialog). The unlock dialog and backdrop/Esc dismissal were not exercised. Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Nav actions: Continue enters the draft builder once the pull finishes; Preview renders the current draft read-only as it will publish; View opens a published month's locked snapshot in the same rendering; Preview and View share one component.
criteria.note: Preview (#mbr/preview) renders 'Preview this month's MBR — A read-only preview of the current draft, rendered as it will publish' in the identical 'Locked MBR' presentation used by the View route (#locked/2026-07-27.0), with a 'Back to builder' link; Continue to builder sits on the collect screen.
criteria.impactWhy: The nav actions are high because they connect the collect, build, preview and publish stages the mission delivers.
criteria.reason: Impact high because these tie the stages together. I opened #mbr/preview and #locked/2026-07-27.0; both render the same read-only Locked MBR component (preview from draft, View from snapshot) and Preview backs out without locking (evidence: preview). Outcome: worked.

criteria.reason: Impact low because it is a polish call. I read the toolbar elements on #mbr/build; I saw no builder-local theme toggle, only the global app toggle (evidence: mbr-build, themeBtn present:false). Outcome: worked.

escalations: This build's data set has zero automatable KPIs — every one of the 19 KPIs is manual (the collect screen reads '6 manual', '3 manual', '2 manual', '3 manual', '5 manual'). Because of that, three automation-dependent surfaces could not be seen at all: the amber refresh-all box (prd-5 / t-011), the wired 'Auto' value cells with Collect/Re-collect controls (prd-10 / t-008), and re-pull behaviour (prd-15). Deciding whether to accept these unverified, or to re-run Verify against a data set that includes at least one automated KPI, is the captain's call.
The unlock-month dialog (t-012-ac5) was never captured in any shot, so its month-only shape and absence of a note field remain unverified.
alsoChecked: The whole project test suite is green: 100 test files, 597 tests passed in ~32s (tests.json, outcome 'passed').
Every KPI shows a purple 'Carried' pill, which is internally consistent with a pull that returned zero fresh values across all buckets.
The observations pass found nothing (observations.json is empty), so no crowding/overflow/misalignment was flagged on the captured screens.
The global app 'Dark' theme toggle sits top-right on every screen and is the single theme source, consistent with dropping the builder-local toggle.
summary: Captain, your rebuilt MBR flow holds together end to end: the Reviews entry screen, the collection step, the builder, the lock/discard dialogs, the read-only Preview and the published View all match the mockup's layout, wording and transitions, and every high-impact criterion I could reach worked. The per-month lock, the insight-completeness gate ('16 of 19 KPIs · 3 still empty'), the Carried pills, cohort deltas and the X off-track marker are all present and correct. The one real caveat: this build's data has no automated KPIs, so the refresh-all box, the wired 'Auto'/Collect cells and re-pull could not be observed at all — they are untested, not broken.
